---
title: "K-means Clustering, Without the Jargon"
date: 2026-05-20
categories: [machine learning, clustering]
description: "How K-means actually decides where the groups are."
---

K-means clustering groups data points by repeating two simple steps until nothing changes:

1. **Assign** each point to its nearest cluster center.
2. **Update** each cluster center to the average of the points assigned to it.

That's the whole algorithm. The tricky parts in practice are usually:

- **Choosing k** (the number of clusters) — the "elbow method" and silhouette scores are
  common starting points, but domain knowledge often matters more.
- **Scaling your features first** — K-means uses distance, so a variable measured in the
  thousands will dominate one measured in decimals unless you standardize.
- **Initialization matters** — K-means++ initialization avoids a lot of the bad-luck
  clustering that plain random starts can produce.
